_comment: This is rulesync 9.6.3's CANONICAL schema, not Claude Code's native one. The event key is camelCase `preToolUse` (rulesync maps it to `PreToolUse` on generate), and each definition is FLAT -- matcher/type/command as siblings -- because rulesync builds the nested {matcher, hooks:[{type,command}]} shape itself. Feed it Claude Code's native PascalCase/nested shape and rulesync skips the event AND silently drops the command: that is how this file shipped inert once already. The top-level `hooks` record is required by rulesync's Zod schema even though only the claudecode override carries content; omit it and generate prints a Zod error, says 'All files are up to date', writes nothing, and exits 0. AGAINST A HUMAN EDIT, tests/test_hooks_wiring.py pins this shape and this comment is only a courtesy. AGAINST A RULESYNC VERSION BUMP, this comment is the ONLY defence: the test asserts THIS file, so a rulesync that renamed `preToolUse` or re-nested the definitions would leave the suite green while generate silently dropped the command and the guard went inert. Re-verify the emitted .claude/settings.json by hand when changing the pinned version in package.json.
